action: Inspected exactly one as-yet-uncovered Chat-exposed externally visible write surface, GitHub create_file, using the already-exposed connector schema only. No GitHub external write was invoked by the semantic probe.

tested_surface.name: GitHub create_file via repository contents API
schema_observations: The caller selects the repository path, so the effect has a deterministic caller-chosen identity at repository/path scope.

The connector contract says the target path must not already exist and directs replacement of an existing path to a distinct update_file operation; this is an explicit create-if-absent style precondition for this surface.
The create call exposes no separate caller-controlled idempotency key or request token.

Under acknowledgement loss, replaying create_file against the same deterministic path is not specified to create a renamed sibling or a second path; recovery can instead read that exact path and compare the stored content to the expected operation payload before deciding whether any retry is admissible.
This schema-level convergence property is narrower than general exactly-once external side effects and does not establish atomicity across a prior checkpoint CAS plus the subsequent GitHub create.
tested_surface.reason: GitHub create_file exposes a deterministic caller-chosen effect identity and a path-must-not-exist creation precondition, which is materially stronger for acknowledgement-loss recovery than previously inspected rename-on-collision or no-idempotency surfaces. However the externally visible effect is persisted in hosted repository storage, and no cross-resource transaction binds a prior Chat-native checkpoint CAS/readback atomically to the later create. The current Phase-1 root therefore cannot count this surface alone as a zero-hosted-storage, richer-mode-parity solution.
tested_surface.scope_limit: Connector-schema-only result for GitHub create_file. No claim is made about undocumented GitHub REST behavior, billing/quota policy beyond the current control constraint, other GitHub write operations, or non-repository side effects. No semantic-probe external file was created.

candidate_protocol: Derive an operation_id and deterministic target path before any external effect.
CAS/update the role-local checkpoint to record the intended operation and exact expected payload hash, then exact-read back that checkpoint.
Only after successful checkpoint readback, issue create_file to the deterministic path.
If acknowledgement is lost, read the exact target path: matching content means the effect is already present; absence permits a retry; mismatching content is a conflict and forbids blind retry.
architecture_implication.proved_by_this_slice: The GitHub create_file schema supplies the deterministic-path and create-if-absent pieces needed for the recovery portion of this protocol.
architecture_implication.not_proved_by_this_slice: No atomic transaction spans checkpoint CAS/readback and the external create, so a crash after checkpoint readback but before create leaves a pending intent that a later run must reconcile. This is recoverable state, not exactly-once atomic commit. Generalization to arbitrary external effects is not established.

assessment.hosted_storage_dependency_basis: The tested externally visible effect is a GitHub repository file persisted by hosted repository storage. Current Phase-1 acceptance forbids a route whose accepted effect depends on hosted storage allowance; the repository-transport exception is not broadened here into permission to count hosted storage itself as the parity outcome.
